dispositions.method: Round two of 1807. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The five items round one listed for the owner to decide were read again with phrase searches over all 4,167 pages of 1807 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords, and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_12.json and batch_13.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As in round one: a story needs one printed item found in 7 or more newspapers, counted item by item. Round one admitted every item in 9 or more papers and chose among the items in 7 or 8 to cover the months and kinds of news; this round admits every once-held-back item that reaches 7, as the round was set. The new stories are top-level: the parent stories of round one (Burr's conspiracy, the Chesapeake affair) name their children in their definitions and stay as released.

counted_item_by_item.The Hayti report: 9 papers (NI and ADA 4 February, EN 6 February, NG 9 February, VA 10 February, HUS 14 February, PGz 16 February, NHG 17 February, BJ 20 February). After its first sentences, six papers print the editor's promise to give the constitution 'without further loss of time' and three (NI, HUS, BJ) go on with the account of 5 December. The EN's printing survives only in the older CA transcription. The ADA also printed the constitution (7 and 10 February), a different item.
counted_item_by_item.Wilkinson's address: 8 papers (NI 21 January, ADA 22 January, VA and EN 27 January, NG 28 January, HUS 31 January, PGz 2 February, NHG 10 February). A fuller report of the same address in other words, printed by NI (4 March) and VA (13 March), is a different item and not counted.
counted_item_by_item.MacDonald's funeral: 7 papers (NG 29 June, ADA and EN 3 July, NI 8 July, BJ 10 July, PGz 13 July, NHG 14 July). Fourth of July toasts that name him with three other seamen (EN 7 July, VA 8 July) are other items.
counted_item_by_item.The seamen paragraph: 8 papers (NI 29 July, ADA 31 July, NG 3 August, EN 4 August, VA 5 August, HUS 8 August, PGz 10 August, NHG 11 August). The NI's commentary of 17 August quotes it and is not counted.

not_admitted.The act to prohibit the importation of s: Printed in full 'by authority' in 5 papers: NI 6 March, a VA extra of 14 April, HUS 2 May, NHG 20 October (where RevX shortens it with '...') and an EN extra of 13 November. Its title is also in the list of the session's acts (9 papers, March) and in reports of the House debates on amending it (November and December), which are other items. Below the rule, like the other laws printed by authority in fewer than 7 papers.
